implementation_notes: C is the only language here where the keyword itself is the smell, and the judgement is narrower than 'never use goto': a goto used as a single forward exit to a cleanup block at the end of the function, or as an early exit from a nested loop, is more readable than the alternatives; a web of backward and forward jumps that spans functions is not. C also has the second, larger form of spaghetti — `setjmp`/`longjmp` used as control flow, which skips destructors in C++ and skips cleanup in C unless the intervening code is written to tolerate it. `gcc -Wjump-misses-init` and `-fanalyzer` catch the worst cases; complexity tooling (lizard, clang-tidy readability-branch-complexity) reports the rest.
pitfalls: `goto` to a shared cleanup label is idiomatic C and is not the smell; a reviewer who bans all gotos will push the code toward duplicated cleanup instead.
`longjmp` out of a frame holding a lock is a correctness bug, not just a readability one.
K&R-style declarations and macro-heavy headers add lexical noise that is often mistaken for control-flow tangle.
